topics.label: Introduction and lecture learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This topic contains the opening framing, outlining the scope and learning objectives of the lecture on cancer causes.

topics.label: Cancer etiology, mutation sources, and epidemiological variation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the foundational origins of cancer, contrasting endogenous mutational processes and bad luck with environmental exposures and geographic epidemiological patterns.

topics.label: Infectious agents and oncogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how biological pathogens and chronic infections contribute to malignancy, illustrated through the etiology and mechanisms of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Chemical and physical carcinogens and DNA damage mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how physical radiation and chemical agents undergo metabolic activation to form bulky DNA adducts and induce mutations.

topics.label: Tumor promotion, host context, and mechanistic synthesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how non-mutagenic promotional factors, microenvironmental inflammation, and host developmental susceptibility cooperate to drive cancer progression.

topics.label: Methods for identifying carcinogens and evaluating cancer risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro methodologies used to determine carcinogenicity and assess real-world exposure risks.

topics.label: Conclusion and summary
topics.groupedBecause: This topic contains the closing framing, summarizing the lecture's core themes on environmental cancer causation and concluding the session.
